definition: A competition mathematics benchmark used across 17 sources, most often as a training corpus and as the full set from which the 500-problem evaluation subset is drawn. In the archive it appears mainly as one column among five or seven, and the useful observations about it are comparative. It is where per-benchmark orderings most often contradict the average: one method with the best overall score loses it narrowly (67.22 against 67.40) while winning three others, and another reports its baseline taking it at one scale (84.0 against 84.2) while the average goes the other way. Ablations are task-dependent on it in a way that is informative -- on one method the largest loss on a grade-school set is removing thought-matching while on this one it is removing the latent thought entirely, so what a component contributes depends on the difficulty of the set it is measured on. Several sources train on it and evaluate transfer elsewhere, which means their generalisation claims rest on a mathematics-only training distribution; a number of them say so explicitly as a limitation.

evidence.note: Reaches test-time scaling with two simple ingredients: supervised finetuning on 1,000 curated reasoning traces, and 'budget forcing', which controls thinking length by cutting generation off or appending 'Wait' to extend it.
evidence.title: s1: Simple test-time scaling

evidence.note: Estimates what a continuous latent thought is worth by freezing the context after it and averaging the rewards of several answers sampled from that fixed context, then credits latent positions with the resulting thought-level advantage and answer positions with the ordinary group-relative one.
evidence.title: Latent Thought Credit: Multi-Answer Credit Assignment for Latent Reasoning

evidence.note: Treats a policy's per-problem failure probability as a random variable over the problem distribution and shows that REINFORCE, pass@K training and MaxRL each optimize a single moment of it, then proposes minimizing the first T moments jointly — which is exactly minimizing the expected truncated number of rollouts needed to reach a first success.
evidence.title: Beyond the Mean: Multi-Moment Policy Optimization for LLM Reasoning

evidence.note: Diagnoses label-free RLVR's collapse as a shortcut in which the same answer-level consensus signal both estimates the reward and receives the gradient, and fixes it by masking the answer span from updates entirely — so a reward can only be raised by improving the reasoning that produces the answer.
evidence.title: Don't Peek at the Answer: Outcome-Masked Group Relative Policy Optimization for Label-Free RLVR

evidence.note: Shows that GRPO's per-completion uniformity is frequency-skewed once credit is aggregated by solution structure — a recurring correct form accumulates positive coefficient mass proportional to how often it is sampled — and rebalances it by a rarity exponent over a partition built from deterministic cue signatures rather than a judge model.
evidence.title: When Correct Solutions Repeat: Rarity-Aware Credit Redistribution for GRPO

evidence.note: Allocates test-time samples per prompt with a fuzzy controller over human-readable difficulty and confidence signals, and — under a selector-matched protocol that isolates the budget policy from the answer selector — reports the result honestly as an accuracy-compute tradeoff rather than an accuracy gain.
evidence.title: Interpretable Adaptive Sampling for LLM Test-Time Scaling

evidence.note: Separates hallucination into a reasoning failure and a knowledge failure, treats the first with a structured reflect-before-answering format and the second with a reward for abstaining when no sampled chain succeeds, and shows the two mechanisms are not interchangeable -- reflection alone never abstains, abstention alone never lowers the hallucination proxy.
evidence.title: REIN: Bridging the Gap between Reasoning and Reliability via Reflection and Abstention Alignment

evidence.note: Identifies degenerate agreement -- students reaching near-perfect token agreement with a teacher by looping while the response as a whole is broken -- and replaces the agreement objective with two directional mismatch corrections, one bounding runaway excess tokens and one injecting teacher-preferred mass at positions the student almost never samples.
evidence.title: Mismatch Matters: On-Policy Distillation Beyond Token Agreement

evidence.note: Tests whether systems that translate natural-language reasoning steps into Lean preserve invalidity as well as validity, by automatically perturbing steps to make them wrong, and finds pervasive silent correction -- with the systems best at preserving valid inputs the most likely to repair invalid ones.
evidence.title: FaithformBench: Benchmarking Faithfulness of Mathematical Chain-of-Thought Autoformalisation

evidence.note: Trains self-correction as a step-level preference problem -- preferring a detect-and-repair continuation over the continuation that would follow if the error went unaddressed -- after first initialising with ordinary step-level preference optimisation, and finds that correcting more often and detecting more errors both anti-correlate with accuracy.
evidence.title: Reinforcing Step-level Reasoning for Effective Self-Correction in LLMs

evidence.note: Gives a search agent an explicitly reversible trajectory tree with reflect and backtrack as first-class actions, and trains the reflection policy with a dense local signal distilled from a teacher that can see the whole trajectory alongside the sparse terminal reward the local decision is ultimately judged by.
evidence.title: LoongReflect: Boosting Long-Horizon Reflection in Search Agents via Global Perspective Distillation

evidence.note: Uses elliptical bonuses over a language model's own hidden-state representations as a diversity signal, validates it in a clean inference-time selection setting, then transfers the same signal into RL post-training — where it eliminates the diversity collapse that degrades pass@k at large k.
evidence.title: Representation-Based Exploration for Language Models: From Test-Time to Post-Training

evidence.note: Tracks mutual information between each reasoning step's representation and the correct answer, finds it spikes at sparse 'MI peaks' that decode to reflective tokens like 'Wait' and 'Hmm', and shows suppressing exactly those tokens degrades reasoning while suppressing equally many others does not.
evidence.title: Demystifying Reasoning Dynamics with Mutual Information: Thinking Tokens are Information Peaks in LLM Reasoning

evidence.note: Finds that the </think> token aggregates the reasoning chain in deep layers and that attention paid to it from that position ranks which steps matter, then uses that ranking to drive a four-operator compression search — cutting 58% of tokens with accuracy holding.
evidence.title: CRISP: Compressing Redundancy in Chain-of-Thought via Intrinsic Saliency Pruning

evidence.note: TRACED scores a reasoning chain by the geometry of its hidden-state trajectory -- net displacement as progress and curvature as stability -- and uses the two as features for a Gaussian classifier that separates correct from incorrect chains without reading the text.
evidence.title: Beyond Scalars: Evaluating and Understanding LLM Reasoning via Geometric Progress and Stability

evidence.note: Formalizes 'spend test-time compute well' as a meta-reinforcement-learning problem — treating one long output stream as a sequence of episodes and scoring it by cumulative regret over tokens — and trains against a dense progress bonus that outcome-only reward cannot express.
evidence.title: Optimizing Test-Time Compute via Meta Reinforcement Fine-Tuning

evidence.note: Introduces EDIS, a trajectory-level score that measures how unstably token entropy evolves during generation, and uses it to select better reasoning rollouts at inference and to curate training samples in RL.
evidence.title: EDIS: Diagnosing LLM Reasoning via Entropy Dynamics

name: MATH
